sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS THE CNTRL GULF CST REGION
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM THE UPR OH VLY TO NRN NEW ENGLAND...

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPR MS VLY SHORTWAVE TROUGH EXPECTED TO FURTHER AMPLIFY AS IT CONTINUES ESE ACROSS THE UPR GRT LKS/MID MS VLY THIS PERIOD. SATELLITE SUGGESTS THAT THE SYSTEM ALREADY IS BEGINNING TO IMPACT HYBRID T.S. LEE NOW OVER THE LA CST. THIS INTERACTION SHOULD INCREASE LATER TODAY/TNGT...WITH THE MAIN RESULT LIKELY BEING SOME DEGREE OF ELONGATION AND/OR NEWD MOVEMENT OF THE MID/UPR LVL CIRCULATIONS OF LEE. LEE/S LOW LVL CENTER MAY...HOWEVER...BE SLOWER TO RESPOND...AND SHOULD STILL BE OVER SE LA BY 12Z MON PER NHC AND ECMWF/GFS FORECASTS. AT LWR LVLS...SFC LOW ATTENDANT TO THE MS VLY TROUGH WILL TRACK FROM N OF LK HURON TO THE LWR ST LAWRENCE VLY...WHILE THE TRAILING COLD FRONT PROGRESSES STEADILY E/SE ACROSS THE LWR GRT LKS AND THE OH AND LWR TN VLYS...AND S ACROSS TX. THE FRONT...AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES TO ITS S AND E...WILL BE THE MAIN FOCI FOR STRONG/SVR TSTMS THIS PERIOD...ASIDE FROM T.S. LEE.

sections.title: CNTRL GULF CST TODAY THROUGH EARLY MON
sections.text: T.S. LEE EXPECTED TO DRIFT SLOWLY N OR NNE ACROSS SRN/SE LA THROUGH EARLY MON. WITH LITTLE CHANGE IN INTENSITY EXPECTED...RELATIVELY BROAD CURRENT OF MODERATE TO STRONG LOW LVL SSELY FLOW IN ERN QUADRANT OF SYSTEM SHOULD ALLOW BOUNDARY LAYER TO FURTHER MOISTEN N OR NNWWD INTO SRN/CNTRL MS AND WRN AL. AT THE SAME TIME...DRY SLOT AND ASSOCIATED MID/UPR LVL VORT MAX NOW MOVING INTO S SIDE OF LEE WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE NE ACROSS THE REGION. TOGETHER...THESE FACTORS MAY SUPPORT A DIURNAL INCREASE IN THE STRENGTH OF EXISTING CONVECTION/STORMS...AND THE ATTENDANT THREAT FOR LOW LVL MESOCYCLONES/TORNADOES. THIS THREAT APPEARS GREATEST FROM SE LA INTO S CNTRL MS AND SW AL /REF WW 832/. THE POTENTIAL FOR TORNADOES LIKELY WILL PERSIST INTO TNGT/EARLY MON...AND MAY SPREAD FARTHER N AND E ACROSS PARTS OF AL AND THE FL PANHANDLE...AS ELONGATION OF THE MID AND UPR LVL PORTIONS OF LEE SUPPORTS SOME STRENGTHENING...BROADENING...AND VEERING OF ITS ASSOCIATED LLJ.

sections.title: UPR OH VLY TO NRN NEW ENGLAND TODAY/TNGT
sections.text: POCKETS OF MODERATE INSTABILITY /WITH SBCAPE TO 2000 J PER KG/ SHOULD DEVELOP WITH SFC HEATING ALONG AND AHEAD OF COLD FRONT CROSSING THE NERN STATES. CLOUDS AND OUTFLOW FROM OVERNIGHT STORMS WILL SHUNT THE EFFECTIVE FRONT S AND E OF THE SYNOPTIC BOUNDARY IN MOST AREAS...WITH THE GREATEST DESTABILIZATION...AND SUBSEQUENT STORM DEVELOPMENT...EXPECTED FROM NRN WV/SE OH NEWD INTO VT BY MID/LATE AFTN. POSITIVE TILT OF UPR TROUGH WILL KEEP THE STRONGEST VERTICAL SHEAR AND FORCING FOR ASCENT W OF THE FRONT. BUT BELT OF 30-40 KT WSWLY 700-500 MB FLOW WILL PROVIDE AMPLE DEEP SHEAR FOR SUSTAINED STORMS AND A FEW SUPERCELLS...ESPECIALLY FROM NW PA INTO UPSTATE NY AND NRN NEW ENGLAND. THE STORMS LIKELY WILL PRODUCE LOCALLY DMGG WIND AND MARGINALLY SVR HAIL AS THEY ORGANIZE INTO SMALL CLUSTERS/BANDS. A TORNADO OR TWO ALSO MAY OCCUR OVER NRN NY AND NRN NEW ENGLAND....WHERE LOW LVL HELICITY WILL BE SLIGHTLY ENHANCED CLOSER TO SFC LOW. THE SVR THREAT SHOULD DIMINISH WITH DIURNAL COOLING EARLY TNGT...ALTHOUGH SPORADIC INSTANCES OF DMGG WIND AND LOCALLY HEAVY RAIN MAY PERSIST INTO EARLY MON OVER ERN NY/NRN NEW ENGLAND. ..CORFIDI/GARNER.. 09/04/2011

sections.title: NERN STATES
sections.text: POSITIVE-TILT UPR SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL UNDERGO FURTHER AMPLIFICATION AS IT MOVES ACROSS THE GRTLKS AND OH VLY REGIONS THROUGH TONIGHT. AHEAD OF THE TROUGH...SWLY LOW/MID-LVL FLOW HAS TRANSPORTED SUBSTANTIAL MOISTURE NEWD WITH SFC DEW POINTS IN THE MID 60S TO LWR 70S AS FAR N AS SRN QB AND CNTRL NEW ENGLAND. 12Z RAOBS INDICATE NERN FRINGE OF A MODEST EML /MID-LVL LAPSE RATES OF 6.5-7.2 DEG C PER KM/ EDGING INTO AT LEAST CNTRL NY. THIS COMBINED WITH A WEAK LEAD SHORTWAVE TROUGH EJECTING NEWD ACROSS ERN NY HAS BEEN TIED WITH LARGELY ELEVATED BAND OF TSTMS ALREADY THIS MORNING FROM VT SWD INTO NERN PA. NRN PART OF THE BAND WILL LIKELY CONTINUE TO MOVE ENE IN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY 1500 MLCAPE AND 35 KTS OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR OVER NH AND WRN MAINE AND COULD POSE A THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND DMGG WINDS. MEANWHILE...UPSTREAM...PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH/DIFFERENTIAL HEATING BOUNDARIES FROM THE MID-OH VLY NEWD INTO UPSTATE NY WILL PROVIDE FOCI FOR ADDITIONAL STORMS THIS AFTN. MODIFICATION OF 12Z SOUNDINGS SUGGEST THAT SFC TEMPS WILL NEED TO WARM INTO AT LEAST THE MID 80S BEFORE MLCINH IS ERASED FOR SFC-BASED STORMS. PER VSB SATL...THIS APPEARS MOST LIKELY TO OCCUR OVER CNTRL PA NEWD INTO UPSTA

sections.title: CNTRL/ERN GULF COAST REGION
sections.text: TS LEE WILL MAINTAIN A SLOW TRANSLATION NWD ACROSS ERN LA THIS AFTN/TONIGHT. SMALL-SCALE DISTURBANCE THAT HAS BEEN ROTATING ABOUT THE LARGER-SCALE CIRCULATION HAS BEEN LARGELY RESPONSIBLE FOR INCREASING TSTMS CLOSE TO THE CENTER OF LEE OVER FAR SE LA INTO SRN MS. VSB SATL SUGGESTS THAT AIR MASS WILL HEAT RAPIDLY IN THIS REGION THIS AFTN RESULTING IN MLCAPES OF 2000-2500 J/KG. RESIDENT LOW LCL ENVIRONMENT AND PRESENCE OF 200-250 M2/S2 0-1KM SRH WILL ENHANCE BRIEF SUPERCELL POTENTIAL WITH ATTENDANT TORNADO THREATS. THE TORNADIC POTENTIAL MAY SPREAD FARTHER INLAND AND DOWNSTREAM WITH TIME TONIGHT AS THE ALREADY LARGE CYCLONE AND ASSOCIATED LLVL WIND FIELD BECOME ELONGATED UPON INTERACTING WITH AN UPR TROUGH SITUATED OVER THE GRTLKS REGIONS. ..RACY/LEITMAN.. 09/04/2011

sections.title: CENTRAL GULF COAST REGION
sections.text: T.S. LEE REMAINS CENTERED OVER THE LOWER MS VALLEY...ROUGHLY 40 NM NNE OF LFT /LAFAYETTE LA/. PRIMARY TORNADO POTENTIAL REMAINS WITHIN THE NORTHEAST QUADRANT OF LEE...FROM ERN LA EWD ACROSS SRN MS/SRN AL INTO FAR SWRN GA AND THE FL PANHANDLE. HERE...TRANSIENT/ROTATING STORMS COMBINED WITH FAVORABLE BOUNDARY-LAYER MOISTURE AND STRONG LOW-LEVEL SHEAR WILL CONTINUE TO RESULT IN THREAT FOR ISOLATED/BRIEF TORNADOES ACROSS THE SLIGHT RISK AREA. POTENTIAL SHOULD CONTINUE ACROSS THE SAME REGION OVERNIGHT...AS VERY SLOW MOVEMENT OF LEE IS EXPECTED.

sections.title: THE NORTHEAST
sections.text: BANDS OF SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS CONTINUE NEAR AND AHEAD OF THE SURFACE COLD FRONT...WITH THE STRONGEST STORMS EXTENDING FROM SRN ME SWWD TO NRN PA. WEAKER SHEAR WITH SWWD EXTENT FROM PA INTO THE TN VALLEY REGION SUGGESTS ONLY ISOLATED HAIL/WIND POTENTIAL...BUT GREATER HAIL/WIND THREAT FROM NERN PA NWD WARRANTS CONTINUATION OF THE ONGOING SLIGHT RISK AREA. SEVERE THREAT WILL GRADUALLY DIMINISH INTO THIS EVENING...AS BOUNDARY-LAYER AIRMASS COOLING/STABILIZATION COMMENCES. ..GOSS.. 09/04/2011 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1127 AM CDT SUN SEP 04 2011/

sections.title: CENTRAL GULF COAST
sections.text: CENTERED NEAR THE LA/SOUTHWEST MS BORDER AT MID-EVENING...TROPICAL STORM LEE WILL CONTINUE TO SLOWLY MOVE/EVENTUALLY SHIFT A BIT EASTWARD THROUGH TONIGHT...REFERENCE NHC FORECASTS FOR THE LATEST DETAILS. LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING AND A LESS PRONOUNCED DRY SLOT WILL HINDER BUOYANCY PROGRESSIVELY INLAND...BUT PERSISTENCE OF FAVORABLE SHEAR/SRH WITHIN THE LOWEST 1-2 KM WILL CONTINUE AN ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT THROUGH THE NIGHT. GIVEN THE COMBINATION OF LOW LEVEL SRH AND THE MAIN MOIST/INSTABILITY INFLUX...THE RELATIVELY HIGHEST TORNADO POTENTIAL SEEMS LIKELY TO PERSIST ACROSS AREAS FAR SOUTHEAST LA/SOUTHERN MS TO SOUTHWEST AL/WESTERN FL PANHANDLE.

sections.title: NORTHEAST STATES/NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: SEVERAL LINEAR CLUSTERS...INCLUDING A FAIRLY EXTENSIVE CONVECTIVE LINE ACROSS EASTERN PA/SOUTHEAST NY...WILL CONTINUE TO POSE AN ISOLATED WIND DAMAGE/PERHAPS SOME HAIL THREAT ACROSS THE NORTHEAST STATES/COASTAL NEW ENGLAND THIS EVENING. HOWEVER...THIS WILL GENERALLY BE ON AN INCREASINGLY MARGINAL/ISOLATED BASIS AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER COOLS/BECOMES CONVECTIVELY OVERTURNED. FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION...SEE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 2127. ..GUYER.. 09/05/2011
